description: Utility to simplify running applications in docker containers

summary.one_liner: A Go command-line utility that generates config files from templates and environment variables, tails log files to stdout/stderr, and waits for network services before starting a container's main process.
summary.what_it_does: dockerize renders Go text/template files into configuration files at container startup, using environment variables and built-in helper functions such as default, split, replace, jsonQuery, and loop. It can tail one or more log files to STDOUT and/or STDERR so application logs appear in docker logs. It can block startup until a file, TCP/TCP4/TCP6, HTTP(S), or unix socket target is available, with configurable timeout and retry interval. It wraps the main application command via ENTRYPOINT or CMD. The README also describes flag validation that rejects options given without their companion flags, and it accepts a directory as a template source.
use_cases: generate config files from templates at container start
wait for a database or service to be ready before launching an app
send application log files to docker logs
pass environment variables into apps that only read config files
poll for file changes when inotify is unavailable in a container
how_to_run: FROM jwilder/dockerize (base image, dockerize is on PATH)
ENV DOCKERIZE_VERSION v0.16.0 and download the release tarball in an Ubuntu or Alpine Dockerfile
notable: Single binary that combines templating, log tailing, and dependency waiting
Wait-for supports file, tcp, tcp4, tcp6, http, https, and unix schemes
Template directories are processed in sorted order
jsonQuery helper for pulling values out of JSON environment variables
Prebuilt binaries for linux amd64/armel/arm64/armhf, alpine amd64, and darwin amd64/arm64
caveats: The README says the -poll, -timeout, and related flag combinations now fail with exit status 1 when the companion flag is missing, a behaviour change for existing command lines
Relative file paths are rejected; file and unix URLs must be absolute
Wait timeouts must be positive; the README notes that Docker itself does not provide this feature
